title: Baked White Fish with Tomatoes, Spinach, and Olives

source.name: Heart Healthy Recipe Guide - HFSA
source.location: Page 12, Baked Fish with Tomatoes, Spinach, and Olives

ingredients.name: white fish fillets (cod, haddock, or tilapia)

steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C). Cut four 12x15-inch sheets of parchment paper or aluminum foil.
In a mixing bowl, toss the spinach, chopped tomatoes, scallions, black olives, orange zest, orange juice, olive oil, and black pepper together.
Divide the seasoned vegetable mixture evenly onto one half of each parchment sheet.
Pat the fish fillets dry, season lightly with black pepper, and lay one fillet over each mound of vegetables.
Top each fillet with a slice of fresh lemon. Fold the parchment over to enclose the ingredients, crimping the edges tightly to create a sealed packet.
Place the packets on a baking sheet and bake for 13 to 18 minutes, testing for doneness at the 13-minute mark until the fish is opaque and flakes easily when tested with a fork.
swaps: Any mild white fish such as haddock, flounder, halibut, or tilapia can substitute for cod.
Kalamata olives or capers can replace standard black olives.
Thinly sliced zucchini or bell peppers can be added alongside the spinach.
notes: Steam trapped inside the sealed parchment gently cooks the fish and draws out tomato and citrus juices into a light, flavorful sauce.

title: Warm Cod Fish and Sautéed Cabbage Salad

ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar or lemon juice

steps: If using salted cod, soak in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain. If using fresh cod, rinse and cut into 2-inch pieces.
Bring a medium saucepan of water to a gentle simmer. Add the cod and simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes until tender and cooked through; drain and gently flake into bite-sized chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and diced green bell pepper, cooking for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the shredded cabbage, oregano, and paprika. Sauté for 5 to 7 minutes until the cabbage is tender-crisp.
Gently fold the flaked warm cod into the skillet with the vegetables. Remove from heat, drizzle with vinegar or lemon juice, and garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
swaps: Fresh haddock or pollock can replace cod directly.
Savoy cabbage or kale can be substituted for green cabbage.
Red or yellow bell peppers can be used for extra color and sweetness.
notes: A versatile one-skillet warm fish dish that seamlessly combines lean protein, hearty shredded greens, and aromatic garlic-oregano seasoning.

title: Pan-Seared White Fish Fillets with Garlic and Lemon

ingredients.name: white fish fillets (tilapia, cod, or haddock)

steps: Pat fish fillets thoroughly dry with paper towels. Season both sides with paprika, oregano, and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large nonstick or stainless steel skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add the fish fillets to the pan. Cook undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes until golden on the bottom.
Carefully flip fillets with a thin spatula. Add sliced garlic around the edges of the pan and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes until fish is opaque in the center and flakes easily with a fork (145°F).
Remove from heat immediately, squeeze fresh lemon juice over the top, and spoon pan juices over the fillets.
swaps: Flounder, sole, or perch work well in place of tilapia or cod (reduce cooking time for thinner fillets to 2 minutes per side).
Fresh chopped dill or parsley can substitute for oregano.
notes: Quick weeknight pan-sear method that relies on high heat and a thoroughly dried surface to develop light browning without overcooking.
